explanation: Compare the middle word with the right boundary. The smallest word remains in the half containing the ordering break, or at the middle boundary.
correctness: If the middle word is greater than the right word, a wrap occurs after the middle. Otherwise the minimum cannot lie strictly after the middle. Shrinking these bounds leaves its exact index.
walkthrough: For [mint,oak,ant,birch,cedar], middle index 2 contains ant, which is less than cedar at upper index 4, so set upper=2. Next middle index 1 contains oak, greater than ant, so set lower=2. The bounds meet at index 2, the minimum ant; return 2 without changing the array.
edgeCases: unrotated input under the stated bank extension.
A singleton or unrotated sorted array returns index 0 under the bank convention; duplicate words and empty arrays are excluded.
timeComplexity: O(log n) comparisons because each step halves the candidate interval; comparing words may inspect L characters, giving O(L log n) character work.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: only three indices and references to existing words.
